Public Version




Jeffrey M. Jakubiak jjakubiak@velaw.com
Tel +1.212.237.0082 Fax +1.917.720.9115




                        CONTAINS REQUEST FOR PRIVILEGED TREATMENT

September 30, 2026


FILED VIA ETARIFF: TOFC 170

Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, NE
Washington, DC 20426

Re:        Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC
           Docket No. ER26-3610-000
           Application for Market-Based Rate Authority
           Response to Deficiency Letter

Dear Secretary Reese:

       On August 25, 2026, Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC (“Applicant”) filed with the Commission
a proposed Market-Based Rate Tariff for the sale of electric energy, capacity, and ancillary services
pursuant to which it seeks authority to sell electric energy and capacity in the Black Hills Power,
Inc. (“BHP”) balancing authority area (“BAA”). As noted therein, Applicant is presently
developing an approximately 1,400 MW natural gas-fired generating facility, and associated
interconnection assets, that will be integrated with a co-located data center in Cheyenne,
Wyoming.

       On September 24, 2026, Amery S. Poré, Director, Division of Electric Power Regulation
– West, issued a Deficiency Letter seeking additional information regarding the application.
Applicant provides such responsive information below following a restatement, in italics, of the
relevant portions of the letter.

        Insofar as Applicant is seeking to close certain financing in early December 2026, it
respectfully requests an Order accepting the Market-Based Rate Tariff and granting the requested
waivers and approvals by November 13, 2026.




Vinson & Elkins LLP Attorneys at Law                                  The Grace Building, 1114 Avenue of the Americas, 32nd Floor
Austin Brussels Dallas Denver Dubai Dublin Houston London             New York, NY 10036-7708
Los Angeles New York Richmond San Francisco Tokyo Washington          Tel +1.212.237.0000 Fax +1.212.237.0100 velaw.com
                                               Public Version
                                                              Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary September 30, 2026 Page 2




1.          Response to Deficiency Letter

       (1)    The Commission requires a market power analysis from all applicants seeking
market-based rate authority.1 A seller can satisfy the horizontal market power analysis if the
Applicant and its affiliates’ generation capacity in the relevant market(s) is fully committed under
long-term power purchase agreements.2

                   (a)     Applicant represents that the entire output of its generating facility will be
            sold on a long-term basis for a term of one year or longer to Black Hills Energy.3 Please
            explain how Applicant fulfills this requirement.

       Applicant clarifies that, as of the date its generating facility begins operating, the entire
quantity of capacity of the generating facility will be fully committed to Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
Power Company d/b/a Black Hills Energy (“BHE”) (an entity unaffiliated with Applicant), on a
firm basis, pursuant to a power purchase agreement (“PPA”) that will have a term of [[BEGIN
CUI//PRIV]]                                                             [[END CUI//PRIV]].

         Applicant further clarifies that neither it nor any affiliate owns or controls any generating
capacity in any other market. Accordingly, neither Applicant nor any affiliate will control any
uncommitted generating capacity and, therefore, none of the capacity or energy of the generating
facility will be available to Applicant or any affiliate (other than as sold to BHE pursuant to the
PPA).

         (2)   To demonstrate a lack of vertical market power regarding transmission, a seller
that owns, operates or controls transmission facilities, or whose affiliates own, operate or control
transmission facilities, must satisfy the requirements for blanket waiver under 18 C.F.R. §
35.28(d)(2) 4 or have on file with the Commission an Open Access Transmission Tariff, as
described in 18 C.F.R. § 35.28; provided, however, that a seller whose foreign affiliate(s) own,
operate or control transmission facilities outside of the United States that can be used by
competitors of the seller to reach United States markets must demonstrate that such affiliate either
has adopted and is implementing an Open Access Transmission Tariff as described in 18 C.F.R.
§ 35.28, or otherwise offers comparable, non-discriminatory access to such transmission
facilities.5




1
    18 C.F.R. § 35.37 (2025).
2
 Refinements to Policies and Procedures for Market-Based Rates for Wholesale Sales of Elec. Energy, Capacity &
Ancillary Servs. by Pub. Utils., Order No. 816, 153 FERC ¶ 61,065 at P 39 (2015).
3
    Filing at 5.
4
 See Open Access and Priority Rights on Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection Facilities, Order No. 807, 150
FERC ¶ 61,211, order on reh’g, Order No. 807-A, 153 FERC ¶ 61,047 (2015).
5
    18 C.F.R. § 35.37(d) (2025).
                                               Public Version
                                                              Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary September 30, 2026 Page 3




                    (a)     Applicant state[s] it will own limited and discrete interconnection facilities
            that are used to interconnect generation facilities owned by Applicant and an unaffiliated
            third party to the transmission system owned and operated by Cheyenne Light, Fuel and
            Power Company d/b/a Black Hills Energy and to a planned data center presently under
            development.6 Please affirmatively state whether such facilities qualify for the blanket
            waiver under 18 C.F.R. § 35.28(d)(2).7

        Applicant has not determined, one way or the other, whether its interconnection facilities
qualify for the blanket waiver under 18 C.F.R. § 35.28(d)(2). On July 1, 2026, Applicant filed, in
Docket Nos. ER26-3119-000 and TS26-7-000, a Request for OATT, OASIS, and Standards of
Conduct Waivers (“Request for Waivers”).8 Applicant respectfully submits that, if its Request for
Waivers is granted, it will satisfy the required showing that it lacks vertical market power for
purposes of being granted market-based rate authority.

         Section 35.37(d) of the Commission’s regulations, as noted above, states that, “[t]o
demonstrate a lack of vertical market power, a Seller that owns, operates or controls transmission
facilities, or whose affiliates own, operate or control transmission facilities, must have on file with
the Commission an Open Access Transmission Tariff [(“OATT”)], as described in § 35.28.” As
also noted above, Section 35.28(d)(2), in turn, grants a blanket waiver to certain entities from the
need to have an OATT on file. But Section 35.28(d)(1) further provides an opportunity for OATT
waivers on a case-by-case basis. Applicant respectfully submits that, as a result, a waiver granted
pursuant to Section 35.28(d)(1) should operate no differently for purposes of a market-based rate
application than qualification for a blanket waiver under Section 35.28(d)(2).

        This all said, Applicant commits to submitting, in the present docket, a compliance filing
following action on its Request for Waivers either (a) noting that the request was granted or
(b) withdrawing the present Application.

2.          Request for Privileged Treatment

       Applicant respectfully requests privileged treatment, in accordance with 18 C.F.R.
Section 388.112, for certain information set forth in Section 1(1), above, regarding the term of its
PPA with BHE. This information reflects “[t]rade secrets and commercial or financial information
obtained from a person [that are] privileged or confidential.” 9 This information is thus
commercially sensitive and not publicly available. Accordingly, good cause exists for the
Commission to grant this request for privileged treatment of this information.

6
    Filing at 6.
7
 See Open Access and Priority Rights on Interconnection Customer’s Interconnection Facilities, Order No. 807, 150
FERC ¶ 61,211, order on reh’g, Order No. 807-A, 153 FERC ¶ 61,047 (2015).
8
 Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC, Docket Nos. ER26-3119-000 et al., Request for OATT, OASIS, and Standards of
Conduct Waivers (July 1, 2026).
9
    18 C.F.R. § 388.107(d) & (f).
                                         Public Version
                                                      Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary September 30, 2026 Page 4




        In accordance with 18 C.F.R. Sections 33.9 and 388.112(b), Applicant states that the
protective agreement submitted as Exhibit C to the Application may be used for purposes of the
present request for privileged treatment. Any questions regarding this request for privileged
treatment should be directed to the undersigned.

3.     Conclusion

       Thank you for your attention to this matter. Please direct any questions to the undersigned.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Jeffrey M. Jakubiak
Jeffrey M. Jakubiak
Melinda J. Warner

Attorneys for Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC
                                  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

       I hereby certify that I have electronically served the foregoing document upon each person

designated on the official service list compiled by the Secretary in this proceeding.

       Dated at New York, New York, this 30th day of September 2026.

                                                  /s/ Jeffrey M. Jakubiak
                                                  Jeffrey M. Jakubiak

CHEYENNE POWER HUB, LLC
                                 MARKET-BASED RATE TARIFF
1.      Availability: Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC (“Seller”) makes electric energy and capacity
available under this tariff to any purchaser as provided for herein. Seller also makes available
certain ancillary services, as provided in Section 8 herein.
2.      Applicability: This tariff is applicable to all wholesale sales of electric energy, capacity,
and ancillary services by Seller at market-based rates in the balancing authority area (“BAA”) of
Black Hills Power, Inc. (“BHP”).
3.      Rates: All sales shall be made at rates established by agreement between Seller and the
purchaser.
4.      Other Terms and Conditions: All other terms and conditions shall be established by
agreement between Seller and the purchaser.
5.      Effective Date: This tariff shall be effective on the date established by the Commission.
6.      Compliance with Commission Regulations: Seller shall comply with the provisions of 18
CFR Part 35, Subpart H, as applicable, and with any conditions the Commission imposes in its
orders concerning seller’s market-based rate authority, including orders in which the
Commission authorizes seller to engage in affiliate sales under this tariff or otherwise restricts or
limits the seller’s market-based rate authority. Failure to comply with the applicable provisions
of 18 CFR Part 35, Subpart H, and with any orders of the Commission concerning seller’s
market-based rate authority, will constitute a violation of this tariff.
7.      Limitations and Exemptions Regarding Market-Based Rate Authority: The Commission
has granted Seller, in Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC, Docket No. ER26-___-000, the following
limitations and exemptions: (i) waivers of Parts 41, 101 (except that waiver of the provisions of
Part 101 that apply to hydropower licensees was not granted with respect to hydropower
projects), and 141 (except section 141.15) of the Commission’s accounting and periodic
reporting requirements, (ii) waivers of Subparts B and C of Part 35 of the Commission’s
regulations requiring the filing of cost-of-service information, except as to sections 35.12(a),
35.13(b), 35.15, and 35.16, and (iii) blanket authorization for all future issuances of securities or
assumptions of liabilities pursuant to Section 204 of the Federal Power Act, 16 U.S.C. § 824c,
and Part 34 of the Commission’s regulations. This tariff authorizes the sales by Seller of
permitted products only in the BHP BAA and not in any other market.
8.      Ancillary Services – Third-Party Provider: Third-party ancillary services: Seller offers
Regulation Service, Reactive Supply and Voltage Control Service, Energy and Generator
Imbalance Service, Operating Reserve-Spinning, Operating Reserve Supplemental, and Primary
Frequency Response Service. Sales will not include the following:
        a.       Sales to an RTO or an ISO, i.e., where that entity has no ability to self-supply
                 ancillary services but instead depends on third parties.
        b.       Sales to a traditional, franchised public utility affiliated with the third-party
                 supplier, or sales where the underlying transmission service is on the system of
                 the public utility affiliated with the third-party supplier.
        Sales of Operating Reserve-Spinning and Operating Reserve-Supplemental will not
        include sales to a public utility that is purchasing ancillary services to satisfy its own
        open access transmission tariff requirements to offer ancillary services to its own
        customers, except where the Commission has granted authorization. Sales of Regulation
        Service and Reactive Supply and Voltage Control Service will not include sales to a
        public utility that is purchasing ancillary services to satisfy its own open access
         transmission tariff requirements to offer ancillary services to its own customers, except at
        rates not to exceed the buying public utility transmission provider’s OATT rate for the
        same service or where the Commission has granted authorization.
9.      Seller Category: Seller is a Category 2 seller in the Northwest region, as that category is
defined in 18 CFR § 35.36(a). Insofar as this tariff authorizes the sales by Seller of permitted
products only in the BHP BAA and not in any other market, there is no applicable category for
Seller in any other region.
10.     Revisions to Tariff: Seller may file revisions to this tariff with the Commission. Nothing
contained in this tariff shall be construed as affecting or limiting in any way the right of Seller to
unilaterally file with the Commission for a change in any aspect of this tariff under Section 205
of the Federal Power Act pursuant to the Commission’s Rules and Regulations promulgated
thereunder.
